items.text: Since we're at the beginning of a brand-new year and Steam decided to kick it off with its Detective Fest, to which both SHINRAI and GENBA no Kizuna were invited, it felt like a good time to type up a little update summary regarding our next project: SHINRAI Saku - Blooming Beyond Despair.

Should this be the first time you're hearing of it, we'd like to direct you towards the previous post with the official announcement. It briefly explains what exactly Saku is and what you can expect from it.
Of course, you can also find more info on its sub page over on our website, along with some introduction cards for the new and recurring cast members.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26014183/b32e86aaf90d1d1b8e46fd6a85c3914a66750220.png"]Now, with that out of the way, let's talk about...
Saku's Progress

We've been quite productive over the last few months, especially in the art department. At this point, there are only a couple more backgrounds missing and mostly facial expressions when it comes to the character sprites.
The script has been fully written for a long time now, but still needs to undergo a bit more polish. There are some more entries missing in the diary and trivia sections of the notebook, though.

The biggest news come regarding the soundtrack. With our previous composer sadly too busy to work on this project, we had to look for someone else to take on the job. And luckily, we found a musical genius of equally amazing talent: the wonderful Crescendo!
You can actually have a listen to her work already, as we've uploaded some BGM samples on our YouTube channel, with the full tracks available to both supporters of her Ko-fi and our Patreon.
Here's a little comparison video featuring a recurring track and its now three different versions:

We're still a little unsure as to how many total tracks we'll need, but right now, we have three out of at least seven. Gonna have to see if it will go beyond that. Either way, the sound category is definitely one that still requires some work, especially since a bunch of sound effects are missing, too.

Other than that, there is also a lot of coding left to do. Unfortunately, our programmer has been buried by a ton of none-gamedev-related tasks which will continue to keep her occupied for a little while longer. Given that she's usually super fast with coding, though, and that Saku doesn't require anything too complex to implement, this ultimately shouldn't result in too big of a road bump.
Potential Release Date

Now that's probably what you're most curious about. Same for us! As always, it's difficult to gauge when exactly the VN will be 100% done, but we do obviously want to release it this year. We'll be celebrating the 10th anniversary of the original SHINRAI's release in August after all!
So, with that in mind, we naturally want to have something really special for the occasion.
Final Words

That about concludes our quick little summary. For more details as to what we've been up to during the past months and what we're planning for the ones ahead, be sure to check out the respective posts on our website: 2025 Retrospect & Plans For 2026.
And don't forget that we keep posting weekly updates there every Saturday. But of course, we'll make another announcement here on Steam as well, once we've got bigger news to share!
Until then, please take good care of yourselves and have a wonderful start into 2026.
In the spirit of "Saku", let's all bloom together this year!

Given that (due to its dinosaur thematic) our next murder mystery visual novel GENBA no Kizuna qualified for Steam's Dinos VS Robots Fest, we thought that this is a good time to post another quick little progress update regarding its development.

The final one, in fact, as the next time we'll make an announcement post here on Steam, it will be to unveil all the release details. After all, we are very close now to, at long last, completing the project!

Everything right up until the point where you need to pick the culprit is fully playable now, meaning that only the four endings, the credits and the extra content is missing. We aim to have all of this taken care of by the end of March. However! We also need to factor in some more time for testing, polish and release preparations, so even if the VN is nearing completion now, it'll unfortunately still be a bit longer before we can share it with you guys. We're really sorry about that...
This project has become a whole lot bigger than we initially expected. It's actually twice the size of SHINRAI now, so hopefully, the amount of content will somewhat make up for the long wait!

By the way, if you want to learn a little more about how exactly GENBA compares to SHINRAI, what the two projects have in common and in what ways they differ, I've talked a little about that in a post on our dev blog. Just the other day, I also addressed the topic of pricing, as we've been asked about that a bunch of times now. The price is not fully decided on yet, but the post talks at length about all the thoughts and considerations going into the matter.

Within the coming weeks, I will start to share more and more in-depth information like this on the blog, along with new screenshots and gameplay videos on our social medias, so if you're curious to see more of GENBA, keep your eyes peeled for those!

Oh right, another thing I'm excited to announce is that we also have an actual theme song in the works now, with vocals and all! Our composer is currently hard at work on completing that as well, along with the vocalist and her vocal mixer. I've already heard a demo and think it sounds super cool and catchy!

Of course, our weekly progress updates will continue on our blog as well (every Saturday), in case you want to stay truly up-to-date. But otherwise, like I mentioned before, you'll hear from us again here on Steam once the release is set! Until then, please take good care and, as always, a huge thank you for your continued patience, support and interest in our work!
Gospel

With Steam's Scream Fest in full swing now and SHINRAI being featured in it, we wanted to take the opportunity to provide another quick update on our next murder mystery GENBA no Kizuna. In case you haven't seen it yet, the store page for it has already been published, so be sure to check it out in order to get a good idea what it's going to be about, and maybe even add it to your wishlist if you want to get notified the moment it's out!
Speaking of the moment it's out, the release is actually the primary topic we'd like to address here, so let's jump straight into it and get the bad news out of the way first:

If you've seen the previous news post or checked out the store page before, you'll notice that the release date has changed. There's still too much left to do to fully wrap up before the end of the year, so as unfortunate as it may be, the date had to be set to 2024 after all.

The good news is that we are getting closer and closer to the end of the project. Script-wise, we are currently tackling the final chapter, the soundtrack is fully composed, and even when it comes to the major art assets, the vast majority of them is taken care of now!

We're terribly sorry about yet another delay, but we obviously don't want to rush anything on the final stretch and risk the conclusion of the project not being satisfying, so yeah... a little while longer it is.

These aren't the kinda spooky horror news we wanted to share, but we hope you'll understand and grant us a little more of your patience (the amount of which you've shown up till now, we are already deeply grateful for). Believe us, no one's more eager to finally see this project up for sale than us!

Now, before we come to a close, there's one more thing I wanted to share with you. The guys over at Fuwanovel asked us for an interview recently (the first one we've ever given), so if you're curious to learn more about us, how we got started with VN development, our inspirations, some behind-the-scenes info on SHINRAI, some more tidbits about GENBA and much more, you can check it out here.

Well, that's about it! Remember, we're doing weekly updates on our website every Saturday, in case you want to stay up-to-date with development, but we'll also make another announcement post here, once we have something major to share.
Until next time, please take care and, of course, have a very spooky Halloween ~°w°~
Today marks the 4th anniversary of SHINRAI's release and, in celebration of that, we've just released a little update for it!

Although no new major content (such as additional scenes or diary entries) has been added, this update applies a number of tweaks and changes to the game, which will definitely provide a better experience. From simple bugfixes and typo eradication to the addition of new music tracks, as well as a much desired checkpoint system for the final chapter.
But let's have a closer look at the changelog, shall we?
(Note: It's advised to start a new game after updating, as the use of old save files might cause glitches)
General Fixes: A number of minor issues such as typos, bugs and visual errors have been fixed.
GUI Adjustments: The textbox design has been updated to better fit with the rest of the GUI.

Sound Adjustments: With the help of our new composer, Solo Acapello, we've tackled a number of sound-related issues. BGM/SFX loops are now seamless, the volume for various sounds has been adjusted, and some have even been redone.

Music Addition: Since some players found the occasional (rather long) stretches of silence to be awkward, new ambience and music tracks have been added to fill the auditory void. In total, there are four new BGMs, one of them being a variation of an already existing track, whereas the other three are completely original compositions.: (If you've bought the OST on Steam, they've been added to it through an update)

Notebook Update: The text size for the notebook content has been slightly increased (yes, it was even smaller before). As a result, all "Diary", "Trivia" and "Clues & Evidence" entries, as well as all character profiles have been revised. In some instances, new tidbits of information have been added, along with references to our new projects. Since some players have gotten confused by it, the "DD/MM/YYYY"-format for D.O.B. information has been changed, as well.

Script Changes: A bunch of dialogues and narration segments have been revised for better readability and structure, as well as to make them more concise and thus improve the pacing a little. Some parts have even been rewritten, while others were elaborated on. This mostly affects the first two chapters and the game's extra content.

Checkpoint System: If you pick the wrong culprit and end up getting a bad end, you will now get a choice between going to the title screen, or returning to an automatic checkpoint that will let you try again. Thus, players who don't save often or overwrite their save files a lot will not run the risk of locking themselves into a bad end anymore.

Code Cleanup: Natsu has taken the time to optimize the game's script, getting rid of thousands of unnecessary lines of code. Honestly, this is something that you, as a player, won't notice. Nevertheless, it makes us feel pretty good!

There are a number of reasons as to why we've decided to update SHINRAI now, four years after its release. Some of the changes are tied to something we can't quite divulge yet, but it will be unveiled within the next two months.
What I can already tell you, however, is that this was also done in preparation for our next two projects:
GENBA no Kizuna and SHINRAI - Withering Without Hope.

As some of you may know, SHINRAI was originally written as a short novel in 2011, never intended to be a VN until 2013. So it's actually been nine years since its initial conception, and ideas for a sequel have been gathered ever since.

Naturally, these ideas have greatly evolved over time, especially during these past four years, while we've been busily working on GENBA and WWH. Thus, I wanted to take the opportunity to update SHINRAI with these developments in mind.

There is also the fact that, back in 2016, when I decided to add some extra content to the game, hinting towards the sequel, it was done pretty much last minute. As a result, it ended up being a little rushed, which is probably why we've found most of the typos in there. Some minor things also didn't quite make a lot of sense, so I wanted to fix that as well.

If you’ve already beaten the game, there may not be enough new stuff here for another full playthrough, but you might at least want to check some of the extra content again, particularly Kamen‘s secret diary entry. She now elaborates more on her feelings towards a certain someone, which will naturally play a big part in the sequel.
So, how is development going on our next project anyway, you may wonder...?

Well, we've made some major progress on GENBA this year, which is still scheduled to be released first. Although it chronologically takes place before SHINRAI, it further sets up WWH by introducing characters, themes, relationships and important plot points.

As of right now, I don't want to make any promises. I can tell you for sure that it won't be out this year, but we have a release date for it in mind, which we'd really like to meet. So keep your eyes peeled for more information towards the end of the year, I guess!

I will talk more about this update, the BBD changes, GENBA's and WWH's development, as well as our plans for the upcoming months in our next weekly blog post. However, before this one gets any longer, I should better wrap it up.

We know that a lot of you guys are eagerly awaiting our next projects and we're really sorry for the long wait. Which is why we appreciate your patience and continued support all the more! Believe me, no one wants to finish these games more than we do!

It's been four years now, and we still receive messages of new and old players on a regular basis, telling us how much they enjoyed our little murder mystery and that they're looking forward to what's next. However, even though we'd love to release something ASAP, we also don't want to disappoint you. So, while it is taking quite some time, please rest assured that we keep working as hard as we can to deliver something that will live up to your expectations!

We're sincerely grateful for all the positive feedback and reviews, the kind comments and messages, and the exorbitant amounts of motivation your support has supplied us with over these past four years!
As developers, we couldn't ask for more ːspumpkinː
